utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Mr. Court Deputy, would you please call at case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is Case Number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. I understand that the Defence has something to raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we've got a number of matters to raise. Your Honours, there is just some housekeeping matters that we have to deal with I think before -- before we start, one of them concerns the -- the tendering of those Zadro statements or the joint statement that you'll recall. We -- we undertook to bring hard copies of that to court; we've got them here and we now just hand those to the Court and to the Prosecutor. As indicated, we will be offering those for tender, but it may be that we can deal with that at the end and not to waste time now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go into the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I make -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I've been reminded that the document D421, the joint statement that we just admitted should be under seal since there are some names mentioned in that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest last night?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We'll try our best to let you go back home today to spend the weekend in your hometown. Yes, Mr. Morrissey, would you please continue your cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Delalic. Just excuse me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, we just have to find a page reference before we start. Very well. I just want to put to the witness some evidence now, Your Honours, and this is on the 14th of February, 2005, at page 55.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. This is in the evidence of the witness Arnautovic, Your Honour. Question at line 4: "Did you return to Grabovica on the 10th of September? "A. Yes. "Q. At approximately what time did you go there appeared who did you go there with? "A. Well, there were -- I don't know. It might have been 9.00 or 10.00. I went with Ramiz Delalic. I set out with him. "Q. How far did you get? "A. We set out from Jablanica. We arrived at a point -- and we had arrived to a point just before Grabovica. That was the first time he was going there. "Q. At what point did you arrive to? Are you saying you stopped along the way? "A. We were going from Jablanica in the direction of Grabovica by car, but there's a kind of barrier or checkpoint in front of the entrance where there was soldiers. We stopped there and suddenly one of our fighters said that he had found two children, two brothers. "Q. This checkpoint which was in front of the entrance and where there was soldiers, was that a checkpoint that was there on the previous occasions when you'd been between Grabovica and Jablanica? "A. Yes. It was a barrier to prevent men from getting in because there was only this one entrance. "Q. How many soldiers were on this checkpoint? "A. There was some in the house and some at the barrier. There were five or six of them standing there -- staying there, I'm sorry. "Q. Are you saying there was a house near the checkpoint and the house were staying in the house adjacent to the checkpoint. "A. Yes? "Q. Are you able to say from which unit those soldiers were? "A. It was near Adnan Solakovic's and there were a few who were to be in charge of the action and a few of ours. And Cedo's Wolves and the Handzar were there before you came to the checkpoint, and the black wolves. "Q. You said a moment ago that somebody had said that he found two children, two brothers. What did he tell you? "A. He said, I found these two brothers in the woods and they say that their grandfather, their grandmother, their mother, their sister had all been killed and they managed to escape. "Q. What was your response and Ramiz Delalic's response to being told this? "A. I know Ramiz well. His response was fierce. He immediately started an investigation to find out what had happened and a who had killed those people." Now, that evidence from Mr. Arnautovic says that you came with him and met the children on the morning of the 10th. Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And he goes on to say, and this is over the page, Your Honours, at page 57 on the 14th of February at line 7 -- well, line 5, actually. "Q. What did you and Ramiz Delalic do with these children after speaking with them? "A. Ramiz lined up the men. He was very angry at the men. He yelled at them and they were all saying, We don't know anything about it, we don't know anything about it. And he was saying, How come you don't know anything about it? He lined up the unit. One of the boys said he could remember the face of the man who killed his family and he would recognise him." So, Mr. Delalic, from that passage that's read out you can see that Erdin Arnautovic said the line-up took place on the 10th. Is that true, the line-up took place on the 10th?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chronology of the events is important. It's not important what time it was. Nobody after all these years can remember what at happened at exactly what time. What is important, however, is what happened there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What's important, I suggest to you, is that Mr. Arnautovic, like other people, say that the line-up took place on the 10th. You say it took place on the 9th. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what Mr. Arnautovic claims. I know what happened and what I have told you here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But isn't it the fact that you knew very well that line-up didn't include a number of soldiers. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've told you, a lot of soldiers were in Jablanica itself. There was some soldiers who were conducting reconnaissance of the terrain, therefore not all of the soldiers were present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But I put to you that you lined up only 9th Brigade soldiers and not anyone from the other units. Is that true or not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in fact this line-up, far from being designed to catch the people was actually designed to protect you so you could say you'd done a line-up and you couldn't find the perpetrators. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see Zuka remove any villagers from the village?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see Zuka cooperating with the police?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you see Zuka being very upset at the death of his own soldier, Ivica Cavlovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which soldier did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Ivica Cavlovic, a man who had his throat cut?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was upset.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Delalic, did you keep the children in the village overnight as bargaining chips in a discussion with Zulfikar Alispago?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because you have a history of taking hostages, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On the 26th of October in the Trebevic operation, you knew because of a radio announcement that you had been relieved of your post as deputy commander of the 9th Motorised Brigade. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And forces led by the deputy commander of the 1st Corps, Ismet Dahic, besieged you in your headquarters. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Ismet Dahic is a person who you've had involvements with since that time as well, isn't he?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But at that time in September and October of 1993, Ismet Dahic was the deputy commander of the 1st Corps underneath Vahid Karavelic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the deputy commander of the corps, subordinated to Vahid Karavelic, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On the morning when he came to your headquarters subsequent to you being relieved by presidential order, you caused your soldiers to go house to house and collect civilians and bring them into your headquarters. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's nonsense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in that tape that was played to the Court, you threatened to Sefer Halilovic on tape that you would blow yourself and the civilians up, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And when you finally came to be dealt with for this crime, it was part of the evidence against you that you did gather this group of civilians around you and kept them in your company during the siege. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was acquitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You were found guilty of insubordination, refusing to obey the order of Dahic and keeping on fighting, despite the order being repeated to you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you ultimately were sentenced to a period of three years or -- approximately three years in prison as a result of that insubordination charge. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But as you told the Prosecutors during an interview, even before that sentence was delivered you were told by government officials that you would be the subject of an amnesty. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You were told, though, weren't you, that you would be the subject of an amnesty. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you tell the Prosecution that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said something else to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What do you say you said to the Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I'd received a letter from the president of the Presidency, or rather several letters stating that there would be a fair trial first and foremost and that everything would eventually be okay, but there was no talk of amnesty or anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What do you think he meant by "everything would be okay"?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Come on. Have a try, please. What did you think he meant at the time by saying to you "everything would be" --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you ask him?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just try to remember. Did you ask, "President Izetbegovic, what did you mean by telling me that it would all be okay?"

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And after that time, Mr. Delalic, did you start doing some work for the government, selected jobs, for the government?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which period of time do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: After your release from prison in 1994.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Among those jobs did you bug the Croatian embassy?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, did you claim -- did you boast in a newspaper article that you had performed exactly that function?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, the question is: Did you in fact bug the Croatian embassy?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I helped bug the Croatian embassy. The simple fact is: I had no access to the Croatian embassy, therefore I would not have been physically in a position to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, in terms of the help you gave, who was it who gave you the instructions to bug or help to bug the Croatian embassy?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, did you say in a newspaper article who it was?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you say it was Bakir Alispahic and a number of other individuals?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You did some work for the organisation AID, as you testified yesterday. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who was the first director of AID?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was Kemo Ademovic for a while and he was succeeded by Munir Alibabic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, but who was the first commander of that organisation?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think for a time it was Bakir Alispahic for a while, but for a very short while.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. He was there for only two or three months. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And then he was removed because of his involvement in the Pogorelica terrorist camp. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as far as you know, he was removed under the pressure of the American government brought to bear on the Bosnian government. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in fact, he's now facing charges arising out of a plan to kill political opponent Fikret Abdic arising from the time when he was in charge of the AID organisation? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was a pure criminal.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, be that as it may -- okay, Mr. Delalic. But anyway, are you involved as a witness in that particular case, the Prosecution against Mr. Alispahic for that matter?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To do with what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: To do with the Fikret Abdic matter. Are you a witness in that case?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Are you a witness in another prosecution concerning Mr. Alispahic -- I'll take a step back from that. Are you --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can we go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Can we go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in 1996 it's the fact that you spoke to an investigator from The Hague. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which year it was that I talked to the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Can you remember the name of the investigator that you spoke to on the first occasion that you dealt with investigators?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I spoke to someone from the OTP was in Hrasnica. I don't remember the man's name, but I do know that Mr. Sefer Halilovic was present, too. The next time I was interviewed, and the interview was taped, I believe it was in 1998 or thereabouts, and the person I spoke to was Mr. Nikolai.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We'll come to Mr. Nikolai in a moment. We're going to deal with the earlier interviews first. Although you can't remember the name of that person, can you recall whether they were dark-haired or blond-haired?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can you remember whether their name was Mr. Abrribat [phoen] or not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Regis Abrribat?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: What about Bert or Bart?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was that meeting tape recorded?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Was Sefer Halilovic present when you gave the interview?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This investigator told Sefer Halilovic to leave the room in which the interview was being conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. But anyway, that interviewer, that person you spoke to, would confirm that Sefer Halilovic was present on the day. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And after that time, you, through a lawyer, wrote a letter indicating that you wished to speak to The Hague investigators and to assist with the investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it's not possible; it's the fact, isn't it? You sent a letter to the OTP saying -- you or your representative sent a letter to the OTP saying that you wanted to talk to them to help them with the investigation. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But one thing's for certain. This was after, and it was to your knowledge this was after, Sefer Halilovic had already made a fuss in the Bosnian press demanding an investigation. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, in due course you were contacted by Mr. Nikolai Mikhailov. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you in fact said to Nikolai Mikhailov that you would provide him with the opportunity to interview a number of witnesses. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in fact you were the one who were able to provide him with a number of the 9th Brigade people to interview. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can we go into the private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we'll go into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm going to show you a statement now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this -- I now indicate we have a number of the statements in binders. As indicated, not every statement that's here is going to be relied upon. Some of them -- it's controversial whether they will be or not, but we have copies and we'll hand those to the Prosecutors and to the Court. And in due course, as we refer to them, the witness is entitled to have a copy of that in front of him when we -- as we go one by one. Your Honours, could I indicate this is yet another act of treachery against the e-court system. We think everything's uploaded except for the -- except for the actual statements, which have been provided in another way. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, just excuse me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm just going to identify the statement I want shown to you, Mr. Delalic. All right. It's behind tab number 9 and this is a statement dated 29th of October, 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I just ask that the witness be shown that, please. All right. So, Your Honours, this is behind tab number 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, do you have in front of you a statement of yours dated 29 October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Pardon me. It's not communication, is it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let me ask it a third time and I apologise for that. So do you have in front of you a statement signed 29th October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. On that occasion, did you say this, and this would be at probably the second or third sentence of the -- of the statement. "When I came to his office," it's talking about Sefer Halilovic, "when I came to his office he informed me at once that with the agreement of the corps commander I'd been given an order to immediately head out with my unit, which is the size of a small company numbering from 90 to 100 men to the Herzegovina area to engage in combat operations with the object of lifting the blockade of Mostar." Now, that's what you said back in 1993. Is that the fact, that it was your job to head out with your unit to the Herzegovina area?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies. I'm not sure where I can find this portion that you've just read out. I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have perhaps --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It might be in the wrong order.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, I think it might be the wrong, counsel, because I -- with my best endeavours I haven't been able to find it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it could be that the witness was given the wrong statement altogether.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: It's not tab 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What's the ERN number?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's behind tab number 11, so we apologise to the Court. And we apologise to Mr. Delalic for getting him to read something that's not right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Do you -- no, you don't have it. Now I try again, Mr. Delalic. Do you have now in front of you a document signed by you dated the 29th of October, 1993?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I'll put that passage to you again. It's three or four lines from the top. "When I came to his office, he informed me at once that that -- with the agreement of the corps commander, I had been given an order to immediately head out with my unit, which is the size of a small company numbering 90 to 100 men, to the Herzegovina area." Now, was that true, that you were given an order to head out with your unit to the Herzegovina area?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 9th Motorised Brigade, or as you choose to call it, "my unit," received orders to prepare a unit of about 100-strong and send it to Jablanica for combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But it's not what I choose to call it though, Mr. Delalic. I'm just reading from the statement signed by you. So is that right, that you had received an order to immediately head out with your unit which is the size of a small company numbering from 90 to 100 men? Did you --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have those orders and I don't know why you're asking me this. I did not receive an order for me to go out with a company-sized unit and to command that unit. I don't know how this came to be written in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, let's press on anyway to the next part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But could we put the English version on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: If they are not confidential material.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, no, it's not. It's acceptable for it to be on the ELMO. Are the copies that we provided to the Court legible or ... It would be better for the witness to have his own copy in front of him rather than having to look over at the ELMO, I think, Your Honour. But Your Honour wants the English version?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Forgive me for a moment, Mr. Delalic, while that's done?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I think the witness should have the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And the English version we'll put on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. All right, thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, the next passage I want to put to you is just a couple of lines down from that and I'll read out this part: "Once we reached our first assigned point, Konjic, outside the corps command, we were returned to Bradina, from which we were transferred to Jablanica. In Jablanica I met Zuka in the command." Now, Mr. Delalic, what's written there in a statement signed by you, that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let's turn over the page -- I'm not sure if it's over the page in the Bosnian language -- it's on page 2 of the English. What I'm looking to now is when you got the news of this massacre. And there's a sentence that begins with the words: "As soon as I was informed about this by Nihad." Can you just look and see if you can find that part, and when you find it, just say -- just tell us that you see it, "as soon as I was informed about this by Nihad."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, now I'll read it to you. "As soon as I was informed about this by Nihad, Zuka's deputy, early in the morning that my soldiers and soldiers from the other units had perpetrated the massacre, I personally went to the scene." Now, Mr. Delalic, is it true that you were informed early in the morning by Nihad, Zuka's deputy, about this crime?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was I what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were you informed by Nihad, Zuka's deputy, early in the morning about this crime?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed about the crime by Nihad, but not early in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Go to the next part. "I personally saw two bodies with entry and exit wounds from a rifle by the Neretva River." Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You told us yesterday there was no chance of you seeing such a thing. Why is that here in this statement?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that when I gave that statement, that was several months after the event, and now it's been already 12 years. That's one thing. And the second thing is that I was questioned about this immediately after I was arrested on the 26th of October, 1993. I was interviewed daily for 10 to 15 hours, but prior to being interviewed I was beaten up so badly that I couldn't hold a pen in my hand. There are records confirming this that you can check. I wasn't beaten as I was interviewed, but when I was taken to the central prison in Sarajevo I was beaten up so badly that I couldn't hold a spoon in my hand. And after that, I started a hunger strike which went on for 20 days. So this statement that is before us now, I can tell you that it is possible that I stated this, but it is also possible that I didn't state this. People were bringing sheets of paper for me to sign. I was -- I gave this statement under coercion. When the commander of the 10th Mountain Brigade was interviewed, he was beaten up so badly that his hand was dislocated; the same applies to his soldiers. I don't know if you're aware of this. You should be aware of this. You should be aware of just the extent of pressure that we were placed under just for being close to Sefer Halilovic. I'm prepared to continue answering your questions, but I had a duty to inform you of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you for informing us of this. Can we go to page 4 of this statement -- that's page 4 in the English version, Mr. Delalic. I think it's likely to be -- just excuse me and I'll find the bit where -- it's a passage beginning -- in fairness to you I'll put you what came first. "I don't deny that my soldiers did not participate in other killings; on the contrary, I think they actually did." Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is that on page 3?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'll just check and we'll make sure. Because of the timing issues, I'll ask you to look at -- so it's page 2 -- I'd like you to look in the middle of page 2, and there's a passage that starts this way -- a passage that starts this way: "That day as I was touring my troops, two children were brought in at approximately 1600 hours who had been discovered hiding in a wood nearby." Do you see that part? It's 12 lines from the bottom, approximately?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So you see that part about seeing the boys at about 1600 hours? You see that part?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, that's what you say today, isn't it? You say -- I'm not holding you to 1600 hours, but you say that you saw those boys at some stage in the afternoon who had been discovered hiding in a nearby wood. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. So the interviewers were writing down what you said in that passage, weren't they? They were getting that accurately, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And the next part is: "There were two boys between 9 and 13 years old. I personally asked them where they were from and how they happened to be there." And that's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So these interviewers were writing down correctly what you were telling them at that part. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, let's move down the page a bit now and come to this part here. "I don't deny that my soldiers did not participate in other killings; on the contrary, I think they actually did, but they were concealing this because they were protecting one another." Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, once again, the interviewers have got that right, haven't they? They've written down what you told them. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that I said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, let's move to the next part I'm interested in. And in fairness to you I'll put in the next part: "I insert that I was incensed by actions of this kind but I was not present on scene with my soldiers when this had been committed." Now, you see that part? Do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't find that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, you remember I read out a part to you a minute ago --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: "I was incensed." Do you see that bit? And in fairness to you now you said that you were incensed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this interview. It's possible that I stated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But that's accurate. According to you, you were incensed and upset. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I stated before this Court is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, let's go on. Now, I'm reading -- it's the very next sentence after that. "After the soldiers found out about the boys, they talked about killing them." Now, I'm going to read -- I'm just interrupting now. I'm going to read quite a long passage to you. "After the soldiers found out about the boys they talked about killing them, because they were witnesses to the murder, in order to prevent this becoming known." Full stop. "I wish to note that most of the soldiers from my unit and the other units were in favour of this." Full stop. "Zuka's deputy, Nihad, was also in favour of this. I was determined that the children be protected and I was supported by Zuka, so that we sheltered the children. And I personally drove them by car to Zuka's staff in Jablanica. Thereafter, they spent six or seven days in Zuka's base while combat operations were underway. I later learned that they had some relatives in Jablanica who took them in and they are still there." Now, Mr. Delalic, that's very different to what you've told this Court, isn't it, what's in that passage. You agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree. What I stated to this Honourable Court is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I notice there's no mention of Sefer Halilovic in that passage there as being present at or approving of any offer to kill these children. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say so anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And if there's one thing that's clear, the people interviewing you were not friends of Sefer Halilovic, were they?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, according to you, all your troubles stem from your association with Sefer Halilovic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in fact, really, your position is that any claims of trench digging or other crimes against you are exaggerated, but to the extent that you did them it was because Sefer told you to. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And finally I'd ask you to look at the -- a passage concerning Sefko Hodzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, this in the English version is on page 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And the part -- we'll just -- pardon me, Mr. Delalic, I apologise for this. We'll just find the relevant passage for you. Okay. So page 3 is the page in Bosnian, and it's maybe 10, 12 lines from the top. You'll see that you're describing actions by Sefko Hodzic and saying that he exaggerated things. And could you -- the sentence I want to start with is one saying: "This was immediately picked up by journalist Sefko Hodzic, who informed the population through the media." Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, the next part is the part I want to read out to you. I'll read that sentence and then I'll go on. "This was immediately picked up by Sefko Hodzic, who informed the population through the media. At the time the objective of such reports was not clear to me. I thought that it was being done because of the negotiations that were underway. However, I now see that other objectives were involved. This had to do with preparations to strengthen Sefer Halilovic's position with military successes and with Zulfikar Alispago as an active participant in commanding these operations being promoted to corps commander instead of Arif Pasalic and Salko Gusic." Now, your claim to this Court previously was that there was a master plan in effect, whereby this operation would be conducted, Sefer's reputation would be restored by the use of Hodzic, and only if that failed would it become necessary to murder Rasim Delic. Do you recall giving that account in court earlier in the week?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But here you are saying in this statement that you only realised later why Sefko Hodzic was exaggerating things. And my question to you is: Have you just made up this master plan that Sefer Halilovic was conducting this operation to get restored, that Hodzic was going to help, and that if all else failed, the Delta Unit would murder Delic? Have you made that up?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan existed, and it was clear to me that certain things had to be done. And all of us were in accord regarding that, that something needed to be done in order for Zulfikar Alispago to be appointed commander. Those two corps were to be joined into one, and their commander was supposed to be Zulfikar Alispago, and Sefer Halilovic's reputation was to be restored. What was not clear to me at the time was that Sefko Hodzic was reporting falsely. When the plan was created, the idea was to seize some territory, to do something specifically and not to lie as they reported during this operation, that certain allegations [as interpreted] had been seized and that the roads were cut off and so on. This is what this was about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, in 1998 on the 15th of January, 1998, in fact, were you interviewed in Sarajevo by two individuals named Nikolai Mikhailov and a lawyer called Karl Koenig, legal advisor or team 9?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What dates?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The 1st of -- sorry, 15th of January, 1998.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998, I did have an interview but I don't remember what month it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, when you were speaking to Nikolai Mikhailov and you were interviewed by him, you were asked a question about an article that you had -- or an interview you'd given to the weekly magazine Dani, such a magazine being printed on the 21st of October, 1997. And I just want to read something from the interview with -- with the Prosecutors here. Were you asked this question by Nikolai Mikhailov and did you give this answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is at page 4 of the transcript provided by the Prosecutors to us of that interview. Q. "Q. I would like you now to tell me about an incident you described in your interview given to the weekly Dani, which was published on the 21st of October, 1997, please, Mr. Delalic?" And you said: "The interview I gave to the magazine Dani I gave only to -- I gave only from the reason to start to write but only the truth and not to write the things that they've written in other newspapers. My intention was to challenge the participants of that event in Grabovica, to make them speak as well, and to tell everything they know about the happenings in Grabovica." Now, it's true you were asked that question and you gave that answer in the interview with Nikolai Mikhailov. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And there was then further questioning about that. You were asked by Karl Koenig: "Is it correct that at the outset you were responsible in some way for the massacre in Grabovica?" The interpreter missed it and then you said: "No." And then Karl Koenig asked it again. He said: "Can I just repeat that because I'm not sure that I think you understood what I meant. As I understand in the press and in the media people were blaming you for what happened in Grabovica." And you replied: "In certain media, but in Croatian media certain media accused me a few times that I was responsible directly or indirectly." Karl Koenig went on to say: "The article you wrote, is that a response to those allegations?" You said: "Not only to those allegations but also in certain independent media in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the same sayings were published. And where few times beside other names, my name was mentioned as well." And Koenig said: "The Grabovica incident" -- no, sorry, he's gone on to another questions and I'll stop. All right. Those questions about the Dani article, you were asked those questions and gave those answers to that -- to the interviewers in that interview. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Could you now be --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness now be shown behind tab number 5 in the folder the Dani article. Your Honours, I should indicate that we -- because we're putting this document to the witness, we took the liberty of getting a letter from the person who took that article, who is now the editor of that magazine. We can produce that if needs be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just before we come to that article there, I've just got another question. You indicated earlier on that you -- that you had possibly sent a letter to the Prosecutors offering assistance. Isn't it the fact that that offer of assistance was made through a lawyer of yours, Mr. -- Attorney Ahmed Zilic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And so that offer was made on the 4th of October, 1999. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No. But it was after that interview that you'd had with Karl Koenig and Nikolai Mikhailov that that offer of assistance was made. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You made the offer of assistance to the Prosecutor, knowing full well you were a suspect in this matter. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is nonsense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. Well, I'll just get a few questions before we break concerning this document here. Could we just go to -- all right. You see you've got three columns in front of you in front of that newspaper thing? No smiling, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the newspapers or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I mean in the newspaper, the middle one. Okay. Do you see this passage here: "I took about 120 soldiers" --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: "When we arrived in Jablanica, we were met by Rifat Bilajac, Zicro Suljevic, Zuka who was the command of the Supreme Command Staff, the special purposes detachment at the time, Vehbija Karic, and a few other people. I handed over the unit immediately, and after that I was at a meeting in order to agree who was going to provide logistical support for our soldiers." Do you see that passage I've just read out?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, that's very different to your evidence now, because now you say you didn't go with them but you went to Konjic. So, can I put this proposition to you again. This stay over in Konjic at Mr. Halilovic or Mr. Habibi's house is an intervention later on to distance yourself even more from Grabovica. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because this is what you told the interviewer, isn't it? The words that I've just read out, they're your words, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A journalist published this interview before asking me whether I agreed with what is stated here. So journalists come, interview, and the regular practice is not to show me what he was going to publish. They just formulate the text themselves. It is not true that I stated this the way it is printed here. I spoke about the general chronology. I did not necessarily state precisely this to the journalist.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, when you say "he did what he wanted," this journalist was a woman, correct? Vildana Selimbegovic, is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not say he did what he wanted. But normally when one gives an interview the usual practice would be to show the interview to the person who was interviewed so that that person can check that. However, that is not usually done in our country. The journalists normally insert their own opinions and so on so that what is actually published is generally not what the person who was interviewed stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know it's the time, but I just want to persist for five minutes, if I might, because it links with something here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let's go on to the next part here. You then go on -- it then says this. "The meeting was chaired" -- and you will recall we just stopped at a point where we were discussing -- where you were discussing a meeting about logistical support and you then go on to give these details: "The meeting was chaired by Vehbija Karic. He was then a member of the General Staff. The chief of administration, Rifat Bilajac, was also a member of the General Staff." And there's some other details I won't worry about, and then we go on to this: "It was re-confirmed at that meeting that Zuka would be the axis commander. The meeting was also attended by other commanders who were tasked with bringing their units to Jablanica to take part in the operation. The goal of the operation was assistance to Mostar. So also there were Adnan Solakovic, Mujo Beglerbegovic, a commander from Dreznica, Enes Kovacevic, the Jablanica commander, the commander of Celo's Wolves, commander of the Igman Wolves, the commander of the Handzar division, Dzeki. Logistics was the only thing discussed at this meeting. After this, I went to Konjic. On Zuka's and on Vehbija Karic's orders, my units were billeted with the other units in the Grabovica sector." Now, that's very different from the evidence you're giving today, isn't it, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are certain discrepancies, but the essence is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, but it reveals, doesn't it, Mr. Delalic, that you are offering a false claim that you didn't go down to Jablanica, in order to pretend that you didn't know where the troops were being billeted and to distance yourself from the crime. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That might be the right moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break and we'll resume at five minutes past 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you once again, Mr. Delalic. Do you have the newspaper there in front of you still?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, I've finished putting that passage to you concerning Jablanica and then going to Konjic. Now, I want you to move a few lines down from that. Do you see there's a part where you say that Vehbija Karic poured petrol on the flames? The sentence begins: "As I was told later, Vehbija Karic poured petrol on the fire." I think it's -- if I could just hold up, I think it might be --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, it's a sentence after that, though, that I'm interested in and it reads like this: "As for me, two days later I got a call from Zuka to go back to Jablanica urgently." Now, that's very different to what you're telling the -- telling the Court now, isn't it, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And isn't it the fact that your story in court now is really a very new story?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did explain a while ago, but I'll say it again. Newspaper interviews are usually not authorised where I come from. An interview is drawn up and then the journalist in theory should go back to me and ask me to authorise it, but this interview was not never authorised. I had an argument with this lady journalist after this was published. In publishing this interview, she made a number of errors and she added some things of her own accord. All in all, if you go through this interview, in essence it talks about everything that this Tribunal is interested in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I'm just going to read a letter to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just circulate copies, please, to the Prosecutors and to the Court? Your Honours, this is an English-language letter and it was written to us in English and I want to put it to the witness now. This is a document dated May the 3rd at Sarajevo -- May the 3rd, 2005, at Sarajevo. On the letterhead of Dani, and it's from Vildana Selimbegovic, editor-in-chief of Dani.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And before I ask you this question, it's the fact, isn't it, that this Dani interviewer not only is Ms. Selimbegovic, the editor nowadays of Dani, but she was also the author of this interview with you. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, this is what she says. "First of all, I am surprised by the nature of your request. Dani is a magazine of some standing in Bosnia and Herzegovina, renowned for accuracy and credibility of its reporting. Therefore, the content of the interview with Mr. Ramiz Delalic truly reflects our conversation. As far as tapes or notes related to that interview are concerned, I regret to inform you that I no longer have them in my possession. Sincerely, Vildana Selimbegovic, editor-in-chief of Dani." Now, Mr. Delalic, can I just put this to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I make it clear I offer this document for tender. There's a number of these, there's two others from yesterday and there's a couple more coming. I'll have to be -- the best thing is if they're dealt with all as a group, but I'll make it clear I'm going to offer for tender. It's one of the things that will have to be dealt with at the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But in any event, Mr. Delalic, the fact is whether or not you came back and checked the contents and dealt with them at a later time, it's still the fact that what she put in here, what Ms. Selimbegovic put in here, was your words, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about authorising an interview. In this case, it was simply never done. What follows is that I simply disagree with the greatest part of this interview. It is a common practice for an interview to be authorised, after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Are you suggesting seriously that a journalist would deliberately misrepresent Ramiz Delalic on an important matter like this?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I am convinced that the tapes are still around; I am certain. They have their own archive, after all. When she says that the tapes have not been preserved, I somehow find that very difficult to believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Well, that letter can be returned please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we need to assign a number to it so that we could treat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honours, could we assign a number also to the Dani article, which I'm going to offer for tender. Your Honours, I offer the Dani article for tender as well, we'll deal with that at the end, too, but it's a different category of statements. Your Honours have indicated to me that you don't want statements to be tendered, and that it's appropriate to read them into the transcript. As long as the Prosecutor doesn't dispute their accuracy then they can form a basis for submissions later. And I accept that. But the newspaper is in a different category, of course, and so I offer that for tender. Let's press ahead now, in any event --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The Dani article dated 24 October 1997 will be MFI 422 and the correspondence from the editor-in-chief of Dani will be MFI 432.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you just so that we keep a grip on this, may I inquire of the Court staff whether we have a number for those other two letters that were offered yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, the letter signed by SR Cesko dated 29 April 2005 will be MFI 424, and the letter signed by Sadika Omerbegovic dated the 15th of May, 2005, will be MFI 425.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, we then move to this -- the next section where you say -- I've just read to you the part where you said: "As for me I got a call two days later from Zuka to go back to Jablanica urgently." And it then goes on like this: "He told me that a massacre had occurred. He and I got in a Jeep and we set off to Grabovica together. There I learned the details from my company commander, Malco Rovcanin." Now, let me ask you this: Did you learn the details from Malco Rovcanin or not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but I can't remember specifically who told me about the massacre and killing of civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, now, Malco Rovcanin and you both fought bravely in the war for many months in Sarajevo and you were close. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what I'm asking you is was Malco Rovcanin there when you got down to Grabovica with Zuka?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the chronology of these events. I'm not sure when exactly Malco was there and I can't say anything about that. At any rate, I went to Grabovica with Zuka. I'm not sure if Malco had preceded us. I'm just not sure. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let's move down to the next paragraph. It begins: "When Zuka and I got back to his base." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it says this: "When Zuka and I got back to his base, he informed his superiors in my presence. I was present in person when Vehbija gave the order for checkpoints to be set up in front of and behind Grabovica so that no one could find out about the massacre." Now, that's a different person giving the order to the one you blame in court now, isn't it, which is Sefer Halilovic. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is taken out of context. It's not the context that I was talking about. The axis where Zuka was in charge and all the other axes had assistant commanders under Sefer Halilovic or members of the Main Staff. And Vehbija was the assistant commander of Zuka's axis and Vehbija was a member of the Main Staff, and Sefer gave an order to Vehbija and Vehbija in turn gave an order to Zuka.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But you left out the part concerning Sefer out of this section here, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that this was taken out of context, what I said. The journalist wrote this as she saw fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's also a little box with a graphic darkening of the text where Vehbija Karic has been interviewed and gives an account. Do you see that? It might be quite hard to read. I'm not sure because the copy we have is a bad one and you may have been given a bad one as well. Do you see that part with Karic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, I'll take you to one part of it and I'll -- if you can't read it you tell us but there's a part in the middle -- I'm probably going to take you to the whole thing, I'm sorry, which I will do. Okay, did Karic say in that interview as follows: "There were no problems at all with the billeting. When I inspected the soldiers, they were happy, having a barbecue, eating grapes. They were billeted there because the axis where they would be used was nearby. There was no motive of adverse situation. I had agreed the billeting earlier on with the locals." Do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that's true, isn't it, that the billeting had been agreed upon between Karic and the local people?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: In respect of what Mr. Karic says in a newspaper, I don't think this witness is in a position to answer. This is what Mr. Karic says in his interview in the same newspaper article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I don't know -- I don't know. If the witness was around at that time or not, he might know or not. But you give a very clear hint to this witness how to answer this question, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sure that would not have been intended in the least. But anyway, I still will ask the question in any event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Delalic, you will have to forgive me. Well, what's the answer? Do you know the answer to that question or not?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in Grabovica when Vehbija Karic visited. I don't know what he said on that occasion. I don't know anything about the billeting, but I know because soldiers told me later about that one sentence he said. I didn't hear it myself, but most of the soldiers did, what he said about throwing Croats into the lake.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, look, this story about throwing Croats into the lake, I put to you that was a lie told by Musa Hota to Malco Rovcanin, who passed it on to you, and that later on it became used as an excuse. Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that there were many soldiers there who heard this. I don't want to discuss the authenticity of this statement now, and you have other witnesses who will either confirm or deny this. What I can say is that I wasn't there myself. Therefore I can't say anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, could I ask you to go over to -- to -- just excuse me, I'll just find the part that we need. Sorry. What we're looking for is a part concerning -- it says: "I also know that President Izetbegovic demanded that the operation be halted." We'll just find it -- you might find it before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The Prosecution are ahead of us and we think it's on page 4 of the Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, I -- we can show you. If you just look, here it is -- mind you those photographs -- well, while you're looking at that, can I confirm those photographs are photographs taken of you at the time of the interview, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Do you have that section? "I know that President Izetbegovic demanded that the operation be halted."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I'm not sure where that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you see where the hole-punched part is on the left side. Sorry, Mr. Delalic, just to be clear, it's -- okay. Now, do you see there that you've said: "I also know that President Izetbegovic demanded that the operation be halted." "Zuka ripped up that order in my presence." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the Madam Court Usher help me for one second, please. I don't know, perhaps the witness has been given the wrong page or if we have got him on the wrong page. Could this just be passed to the witness to -- maybe this will help.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, I'm just going to give you a part where it's marked in green. That's the part where we want.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had the wrong page. These pages have different photographs. I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, now, your position in the past used to be that Zuka ripped up an order by President Izetbegovic. But now in this court what you say is that Halilovic and Zuka ripped up an order from Rasim Delic. That's the fact, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said before this Honourable Trial Chamber is that Mr. Sefer Halilovic crumpled the order and Zuka was the one who ripped it up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, but we're focussing on something different to that. We're focussing on the fact that in the past you said that it was an order from Izetbegovic. Now, you're claiming to have seen a specific document, namely Exhibit 157, the supposed order from Rasim Delic. And what I'm asking you is: Why did you tell this journalist that it was an order from President Izetbegovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't give anyone's name at all at the time, not the president's name, not the army commander's name. I just said that there'd been an order from the supreme command to halt the operation, but I didn't name any names.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you provide as well to this journalist access to or contact with the following people, who then spoke to the magazine: Erdin Arnautovic, Elvedin Husic, a couple of others, one with a wrong name, but I'll come to that in a minute. Erdin Arnautovic, do you see that -- I'll find you the part just so you don't have any confusion. It should be the top of page 4 on the left-hand corner, the top left-hand corner of page 4. Sorry --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's Erdin Arnautovic and that's the same Erdin Arnautovic that we've already asked some questions about. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you put this -- how did -- can you just explain: Did you provide a statement from Erdin Arnautovic to the journalist or did you arrange for the journalist to speak personally to Erdin Arnautovic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No way. I didn't. She knows these people herself. She interviewed whoever she was able to reach at the time. Many of the soldiers were not in Sarajevo at the time, among those who had been in Grabovica. She interviewed all those who still resided in Sarajevo, but it certainly wasn't through an act of intervention on my part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. We'll go now to -- but even so, it was still the fact, wasn't it, that Erdin Arnautovic was a good friend of yours at that time, as he still is today. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we're no longer friends. I haven't been in touch with him for over two months. We even quarrelled. If you look at this interview, you see that it's Ramiz Delalic being interviewed, but other people are being used for the benefit of the interview. She used other people's statements, even Zuka's statement, and some other people, too. If you look at this, you can tell that this is not only my statement. She published things that were said by other people, by Zuka, by Vehbija Karic, and what have you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You're quite right about that. In fact, she puts it in quotation marks, from Erdin Arnautovic. Shall I ask you: Did you quarrel with Erdin Arnautovic because of the evidence he gave here?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Come on. I was not in touch with him prior to my testimony. It's sheer nonsense. I don't think this is something we should go into at all. It was an acquaintance. It was not a friendship in the proper sense of the word. We were in the same war. We fought together, and there's a variety of ways you can refer to people like that, a fellow soldier, a fellow fighter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, then, now, can you go to the next entry, Elvedin Husic, a soldier. Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which page that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It should be on the same page. It's on the same page. I think -- Mr. Delalic, I think it's about there. If you look in this direction --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Elvedin Husic was a person who at that time in 1997 was in fact actually a co-accused of yours in an indictment concerning alleged racketing of Daut Basovic, an indictment which I should point out, you were not found guilty of it. But nevertheless it's the fact that you were co-accused with Husic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know about Daut Basovic and Husic is that Daut Basovic offered 12.000 marks to Elvedin Husic not to give the statement he was supposed to give before the court. You must be aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And go to the next one there. Do you see there's a person referred to as Fikret Hajrovic who was the commander's escort. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, in reality, the commander's escort was Fikret Kajevic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whose escort?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The commander's escort -- well, sorry, perhaps I'll ask you this: He was your escort, wasn't he, at the time of the Grabovica matters?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no, he was not an escort. Only sometimes would he escort the commander, or rather the deputy commander, but not on all occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm not -- these words are not attributed to you, this Fikret Hajrovic was the commander's escort, so I'm not putting to you whether that's got anything to do with whether you were the commander or not at all. What I want to put to you is what this individual supposedly said. "We went to Jablanica with the soldiers and Zuka met us there. As soon as he took charge of the company he said that he would take care of everything and that Ramiz didn't need to worry about anything. I went to Konjic with Ramiz in order to obtain some MTS which we meant to transport to Sarajevo." Now, let me just ask you straight-out as a matter of fact. Is that true? Did you in fact go to Jablanica and then go to Konjic later on with Fikret Kajevic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, the name itself, Fikret Hajrovic, the name stated in this statement reflects just how careful this journalist was when drafting this text. The name that she put here, Fikret Hajrovic, does not exist. She probably meant Fikret Kajevic. Now, what is stated I really can't tell you anything about that. That is his statement alone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, can you tell me whether Fikret Kajevic gave his real name to the journalist?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So you've spoken to him about it then?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't speak to him about anything. It is stated here "Fikret Hajrovic," that's the name in the case. I don't know that person. Perhaps that person exists, but I don't know him. That person was never an escort of mine. If this is indeed Fikret Hajrovic then I don't know the person and I don't know who could have stated something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I want to take you to another document now -- sorry, we're just going to give the proper number. This is a statement made to the cantonal court in Sarajevo on the 2nd of December, 1998, and it's -- excuse me, pardon me, it's behind tab 10, Your Honours. Okay. This is a document that's -- yes -- it's behind tab 10. Perhaps just show us that one. Okay. Do you have in front of you a record of witness interview dated the 2nd of December, 1998, before the investigative judge of the cantonal court in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And on that occasion is the investigative judge listed as being Ibrahim Hadzic and is the recording clerk Edina Djudjevic [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what appears at the bottom on the left, Ramiz Delalic and on subsequent pages. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Would you please turn over to the first page of the text itself. Now, the first passage I want to take you to you will see that you say this: "The unit from my brigade was transferred from Hrasnica to the Herzegovina area, but I did not go with the soldiers on that occasion." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. We'll try to find it for you. It may be 11 or 12 lines from the top.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: "I did not go with the soldiers on that occasion." Okay. Now, there's some more information there which we can go to if we need to, but would you go down a bit further and say -- and look at this: "Malco Rovcanin" -- it's a bit lengthy, but I think I better take you to the whole thing, so go back to where you were. "I would like to point out that before the units went out to the front at Herzegovina, a single unit was formed out of the unit from the 9th Motorised Brigade, the 2nd Independent Battalion, and the 10th Mountain Brigade, to which were appointed the company commanders and the battalion commander who commanded the entirely newly formed unit." Now, do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you go on to say: "I cannot recall now the name of the man who commanded this entire newly formed unit, but I know that Malco Rovcanin was the commander of the company in this overall unit which was formed from my unit." Now, I want to stop there for a minute. First of all, your account in this court has been that Sefer Halilovic was not present at Hrasnica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So who was it who appointed this battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which battalion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The one that you refer to here, the one where you say --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vahid Karavelic was the one who appointed the battalion commander, made up of the Sarajevo units, and he was the commander of the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We've got a problem here because he came to this court and said that he didn't. Have you got a very clear memory that a battalion commander was appointed at all?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Who was that battalion commander?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Senad Pecar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's proceed. Was Malco Rovcanin appointed as a company commander within this battalion that you've referred to, to go down to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I stated then -- or rather, I speculated then and I still am speculating about the company commander. I am still speculating, because to this day I don't know who was appointed company commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, the difficulty with that is that what you said in the statement is: "I know that Malco Rovcanin was the commander of that company." My question is: Why did you say that in the statement?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The problem with this statement is that I asked, or rather I got into an argument with the judge because I wanted the words as I uttered them to be recorded. I wanted them to be recorded directly as I uttered them. I wanted the court reporter to record my words, not judge's words. And the judge made his own account and had those words recorded; this is why we got into a row. I claimed then as I continue to claim to this day that I truly don't know who was appointed the company commander. And that's all I can tell you.
