utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it may be not all you can tell us because the date of this statement here is 2nd of December, 1998, whereas the date of your quarrel with Judge Hadzic was in April of the following year, wasn't it, and we'll tendered that into evidence, that indictment where -- sorry, that judgement where you got in trouble for playing up in court, effectively. The conduct on that occasion was on a different date. What do you remember about that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not create any incident in the court. I simply wanted my own words to be recorded, not the judge's words. And this is exactly what I told the judge in the courtroom. Perhaps you are a judge but you know nothing about the army matters and the orders. This is why I wanted my own words as I uttered them to be recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But you've misunderstood what I'm putting to you. The time when you got angry with the judge was on a different date, Mr. Delalic. This time, here, we're talking about the 2nd of December, 1998. So I'll ask you the question again. Why was it that it's said in this statement, not the one when you had a fight with the judge but this one here on the 2nd of December, does it say that you know that Malco Rovcanin was the commander of the company?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've told you, I suggested to the judge that my own words ought to be recorded, not his words, addressed to the court reporter.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, in the light of that, then why is your signature on the document?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even take a look at what is written here. I signed it without reading. What you are stating here are simply the matters that you are interested in. And what this Court should be interested in, which are stated here, should be true. I can't remember all of the details because it's been 12 years and I continue to affirm that I still do not know who was the company commander. If I stated then that it was Malco Rovcanin, that means that that was my best guess at the time. But I cannot claim with any certainty whether it was him or not. I don't consider this to be relevant at all and I don't see why you keep insisting on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The reason I'm insisting on it is because I want to find out why it is that these words are there on this page, on a page which is signed by you, and that's why I'm asking you the question. And the first question is: If you did not want to sign that page, you would not have signed it. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, during both interviews I got into an argument with the judge because he made sure that his words were recorded and not my words.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, but I understand what you say about that. But we come back to this: You were -- you signed the bottom of the page and what I want to ask you, perhaps, is: Was your lawyer, Mr. Karkin, present when you signed the bottom of that page?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he was present. All I know is that this particular judge was later replaced. And now he doesn't practice law anymore precisely because of this reason and others, similar ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, look -- all right, you want to make comments like that, let me ask you a question. Mr. Karkin here, who you're with here, did he ever supply guns to you while you were in the 9th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, did you make a statement telling -- in 1993 telling the investigators that very fact, that he'd given guns in exchange for his children being placed in the logistics company of your 9th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, you can remember that --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Perhaps the relevance of this could be stated by learned counsel as to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, that's reasonable.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I'm happy to state the relevance of it. It's a question entirely for the Court whether Mr. Delalic and Mr. Karkin want to remain in court while I give the answer to it. But unless somebody says they should go, I'll now commence to give the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe we could save this part of the questions at a later stage or at the beginning of the next sitting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's a good idea. Yes, well, I won't persist with that any further right now. Well, I've got one question, I think, arising from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Karkin --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll demonstrate the relevance. I'll deal with it now, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Karkin was present with you when you were interviewed by Nikolai, is that correct, Nikolai Mikhailov?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Karkin was present with you when you were interviewed by the Prosecutors down in Sarajevo in November 2004. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Karkin was present with you during one entire day of your proofing session here in The Hague. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Karkin was present --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Let me put this proposition, though, the account you've given in court today -- sorry, over this week is an account that you have been rehearsing for years in order to protect yourself for covering up the crime at Grabovica. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you mentioned just a minute ago, I wrote to The Hague Tribunal while Madam Arbour was still here. I wrote a letter to them then, and it was on that occasion that I said that, if needed, I would come to The Hague and would be held accountable. What you're saying, that I practiced and rehearsed this is something that you are claiming. There are many other witnesses who can corroborate what I've been saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Nikolai Mikhailov would be one such witness, wouldn't he?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what he could testify about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, did you take the opinion -- did you hold the opinion, Mr. Delalic, that you were safer inside the investigation rather than outside it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. All right. Let's move down that page further -- or while I move down that page, just excuse me a moment, please, I just want to find where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So anyway, I was asking you about Malco Rovcanin and now I wish to go on a little bit further down the page. Since we diverted on to the Mr. -- on to other matters. Do you have that spot there where we were. "I know that Malco Rovcanin was the commander of the company." Do you see that? It was where we were before. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "Malco Rovcanin, as the commander of the company within my unit." Is that what you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, that's good. Okay. So let's read that sentence. "Malco Rovcanin as the commander from my unit and the other units from this newly formed unit went to the Herzegovina front together with the soldiers while I remained in Sarajevo and set off for this front only two days after the soldiers had been sent. I did not have to go on the same day as the soldiers because there was no need for that. Two days later, as I said, I left Sarajevo together with Adnan Solakovic and I stopped in Konjic while Adnan Solakovic continued the journey to Jablanica with the unit." Now, you see that passage I've just read out?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, that's nothing like what you say in court now, is it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I was apprehended and was in the custody when I was interviewed, I didn't go there voluntarily. I was taken into custody by the police and taken to the court. Judge Hadzic told me that he sent several notices and summonses for me to appear. I didn't know about that, but he said that there was several such notices. And on that day, I was brought in by the police. And as I've already told you, immediately at the beginning I had an argument with the judge because the police picked me up early in the morning and then kept me for hours in some room before the judge was able to interview me, which they were not authorised to do at all. Therefore, I don't know anything about this statement. I don't even remember stating something like this. What I wish to say is that I came to the court unprepared. And actually, what I stated here before this Honourable Chamber is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But what I want to put to you is that when you came to court on that occasion you just had a different false story that you wanted to tell and you told it. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're talking about. What false story?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, let's press on. You said that -- I'll just summarise the next passage. You said you came down from Konjic to Jablanica for a couple of different reasons. And then you said this: "Actually, I also came to Jablanica because of weapons that I had ordered earlier from Zulfikar Alispago, so I came to see what was going on with those weapons." Now, that's consistent with what you're saying in court here today, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So the judge got that part of what you told him right, didn't he?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And just to be clear about this, are you sure it's not -- are you really sure that you were going to buy weapons from Zulfikar at the very time when he was about to launch an offensive in the Vrdi area with an army that was pretty light armed for weapons?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you're asking me about now is something that is currently investigated in the proceedings before the municipal court in Sarajevo. So you can ask information from that court. I affirm that I didn't go to see only Zuka about weaponry. I also went to Konjic for that reason. And as I've already said, there is information that -- there are documents that can corroborate that with the court and also there is the statement that Zuka gave to the court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Delalic, neither tapes, statements, other proceedings, or any other such things prevent you from answering my question. Now, my question is -- and I'll put it a bit differently just so we don't bear cross-purposes. My question is: Haven't you just made up as a false story, this account that you were going down to Jablanica to check up on an arms purchase from Zuka?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Because it's true that Zuka was just about to involve himself in a -- significant combat activities in the Vrdi-Dreznica area. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, now, come on. You do know because you've claimed that you saw that attack order of Zuka dated the 11th of September, which the Prosecutor showed to you. Now, let me ask you the question again. You knew very well Zuka was going to be engaged in combat activities and you also knew that he was short of weapons, true or false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he had sufficient amount of weapons, part of which he was supposed to hand over to me. If we go back a little bit, I -- you'll see that I think that I have stated that while talking to Zuka I asked him to give he the weapons for which I had paid him, and he said something to the effect that he would give it to me after the offensive. And if you go back a little bit, you will see for yourself that I did state that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, are you pointing out that that conversation that you've just referred to is in this statement here? Look, in any event, frankly, I won't argue with you about that topic, Mr. Delalic, now. It's -- what I'm putting to you is the next part now, and we'll go on to it. You said: "When I came to Zulfikar Alispago's command, I saw Sefer Halilovic, Bilajac, and Zulfikar Alispago there and they were already at the time discussing the forthcoming operations." Correct? Now, effectively that's what you've told this court now, isn't it? That's your account now that when you arrived those people were sitting there discussing the war. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So the judge has got that part right again, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And then the next part is this: "While we were sitting there, somebody informed Zulfikar Alispago's base that some civilians who lived in Grabovica had been killed in the Grabovica area." Now, that's different to your account now, isn't it, because your account now is when you got there the news was already known. But here, to Judge Hadzic, you've said, in this version anyway, you said that it was while you were sitting there that the news came in. Now, let me ask you this: Which one of those two accounts is true, the one that you told in court here, or the one that's in this statement to Hadzic, or are neither of them true and they're all just different editions of the false story?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, that in fact from day one when I started speaking to this very day, the essence remains the same and you can use that to prove the truth. These are minor details. It's something that I can't remember. I must have given over a thousand statements. You can't remember every single word and you seem to be clinging to these words. Again, I shall say that what I stated before this Honourable Tribunal is what is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand when you said that you've given thousands of statements, that's just a figure of speech and you're not being literal. But how many statements did you give to Nikolai Mikhailov?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I spoke to him twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, you said you'd spoken to him ten times before -- when we asked you before. But are you saying that you made two statements to Nikolai?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave him one statement, the one that he taped; and the next time we were having a conversation over coffee and I gave another statement. I don't think this was recorded but I gave him an account and a chronology twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And on that second occasion did he take notes?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He may have had some sort of a notepad that he took notes in, something to serve as memos, but he did ask quite a number of questions that he wanted to know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I mean, I'm not -- sometimes I ask you harsh questions. I make it clear that with this one here I'm not putting to you that you're making up these meetings with Nikolai. I just want to know the details about them. The meeting in the coffee shop, can you remember which coffee shop that was?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the Kiborg in Strossmayer street in Sarajevo. It's a cafe that I actually own.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And doing the best you can to remember, is it your best memory that he did have a notepad with him and he was taking notes as memos for later times?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think he did. He was taking notes of some sort. At the same time, he was giving me names that he had on a list, names of people that he wished to interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And did you help him to find those people?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The people he wanted to interview, well, some were around and some were not around; and I told him so. I helped him to track down some of the people. I gave him some phone numbers -- or rather, I gave some of the people his phone number and people called back and they were eventually interviewed. But it really depended. He would leave a card behind, and then if I tracked someone down I would give them Mr. Nikolai's details and suggested that they talk to him if they wished to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand that. And are you able -- you probably don't have the exact date, but can you give us an approximate time of this coffee shop meeting. Was it before or after the taped meeting that you had with him?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember specifically. But most of the meetings took place afterwards. There were one or two meetings before the interview was taped. But most of the meetings occurred after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Thank you for that. Now I want to return to this statement here. Down at the bottom of the -- sorry, at the bottom of our page here -- well, that may be four lines further down, you said this: "I know that Sefer Halilovic ordered Zulfikar Alispago in my presence to go and see what happened and what was involved." Do you see that section?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that's accurate, isn't it, that's the same as what you say here?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what I'm putting to you is a positive fact, assertion, to you that that's true, that at one point -- I'm sorry, I'll withdraw that. I'll phrase it another way. We'll go on with the statement. Now, in this statement, maybe another ten lines further on, you said this: "Already at the entrance to Grabovica when we crossed the bridge and crossed to the right bank of the Neretva River, I noticed a group of civilians, perhaps seven or eight of them, and there were both men and women in this group who had just left Grabovica in the direction of Jablanica on foot." Now, do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You can't remember seeing live civilians walking away from the village. Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's press on. You said this: "On arrival in Grabovica, I immediately headed for my unit where my soldiers were, and from conversation with them I found out that Zulfikar Alispago and Vehbija Karic were in charge of the billeting of all those soldiers in the Grabovica village." Now, is that true that your soldiers told you that Zulfikar and Karic had been in charge of the billeting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said is that they were accommodated side by side and they were there when people were being put up. That's all I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's move down the page a little bit further. And just notice this bit here. "I would like to point out that I stayed in the unit among my soldiers while Zuka went to two of the units that were billeted in Grabovica." Do you see that part?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And you went on to say this: "Apart from what the soldiers told me in connection with their billeting, none of the soldiers said anything to me so that I did not find out anything in connection with the deaths of the civilians, and in particular I did not see any bodies of persons who had been killed."

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't see any in the village itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Oh, I see. What you're saying is that this statement's not false because the bodies you saw were somewhere else. Is that the way you want to put it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them just outside the village, along the road leading into the village but not in the village itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then let's read the next part. This part's a bit longer, so read it with me so we don't miss anything and we'll go through it. "After approximately an hour I returned with Zuka to his base in Jablanica. In Jablanica, in my presence, Zuka informed Sefer Halilovic about what he'd seen in Grabovica. He told him that he thought there had been killings but that he had not seen a single body. The conversation continued to the effect that a check needed to be organised to see whether there had been killings, and if there had, where the bodies were. And that an investigation should be conducted in connection with this incident. The conversation was conducted by Zuka, together with Sefer, and there was some other officers there as well whom I cannot remember now." Now, Mr. Delalic, I want to put two things to you there. First of all, in fact what you put there was quite accurate as to what happened in really -- in real life. You did come back with Zuka, and Sefer and Zuka did say that there should be an investigation. Is that true or false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No one spoke about an investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Why did you say this in this signed statement?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where does it -- where is that stated? I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: We'll find it for you -- I'm sorry, were you unable to follow that when I was reading through? My apologies if -- that's okay. We'll find it for you. Do you have the third page there in about the middle of the page -- in about the middle of the third page you'll see the word "nakon." If you look down the left-hand side column the word nakon is --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. "After approximately an hour I returned with Zuka to his command in Jablanica. In Jablanica, in my presence, Zuka informed Sefer Halilovic about what he had seen in Grabovica. He told him that there had been killings -- sorry, told him he thought there had been killings but that he had not seen a single body. The conversation continued to the effect that a check needed to be organised to see whether there had been killings, and if there had, where the bodies were, and that an investigation should be conducted in connection with this incident. The conversation was conducted by Zuka together with Sefer, and there were some other officers there as well who I cannot remember now." Do you see that passage that I've just read out, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, that's true, isn't it, that when you and Zuka came back from the village in the evening of the 9th of September, Zuka and Sefer Halilovic did have a discussion to that effect, saying that there should be an investigation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they did have an investigation, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just slow down a minute. Isn't that what was said? Didn't Zuka and Sefer say in your presence that there needed to be an investigation after you and Zuka came back from Grabovica? That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did they have an investigation or not? I'm asking you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, look, one of the great benefits of being a lawyer --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only did they not have an investigation --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just answer the question. That's the truth, isn't it? They came -- what you said here is the truth: They came back and said, We must have an investigation. True or follows?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only did they not have an investigation, they asked that the children be disposed of and for the whole thing to be covered up. They failed, however. Not a word was said about an investigation being carried out. And this is demonstrated by Rasim Delic's letter being torn up. There is no paper trail whatsoever to show that any investigation had been ordered at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: How do you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably one would already have been produced if any such thing was around.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Delalic, isn't the true state of affairs, something that you left out of this statement, that when Zuka and Sefer said that there should be an investigation you said "no" and you said the soldiers won't stand for it and there'll be a fight if any investigators go down there. True or false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And from that time on you behaved in a hostile and confrontative way with any civilian police or military police or SVB who you came across. True or false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's impossible to say these things. There were thousands of soldiers down there. There must be a witness somewhere who could testify about these things. This is sheer nonsense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And finally can you account for why it is on a signed statement of yours these words are to be found, and I mean signed by you, Mr. Delalic, not by somebody else?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've told you, this judge, who was later replaced, made sure he got his own words recorded, not mine. And this was the reason behind our quarrel, the fact that it wasn't my words that were recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, look, I've only got one more question on this topic and it's this: Since they weren't your words that were recorded, why did you sign it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first of all, there were several police officers present, the court police. I wanted to leave as soon as possible, so I just signed it to get it over with without even reading the report. I don't think it was completed. It took several hours more, but the process was interrupted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Maybe so, Mr. Delalic, but -- I don't mean this in any underhanded way, but you could take care of those policemen if you needed to, couldn't you, if they attacked you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. That's nonsense.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, this might be the moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break and we'll resume at 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Judge Szenasi won't be able to be with us for this sitting, and the remaining Judges, according to the Rule 15(B) continue to proceed. Before we have the witness, Mr. Morrissey, are you ready to tell us about the counsel kept --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, it's the Defence case that -- Your Honour -- could we go into private session, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes, we'll go to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey, what's your estimation for your cross-examination? I hope you could leave some time for Ms. Chana to do some re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, there are two matters that I'll raise. The first one is that I've nearly finished with this document showing. So I think that's got probably another five or ten minutes. Then I have to deal with some matters at the end of this phase of the operation. There's the order of the 12th I've dealt with pretty quickly. I'm not going to go back to that. Some of the things that happened in Sarajevo before units were sent back down again. I've got to put some things to him because there may be some evidence that goes through the next witness concerning that. I've got some questions about two indictments that are relevant, that is time-consuming but I'll try to do it quickly, and that's the substance of what I have. That's really the -- it's possible to finish. I should have -- I didn't realise how we were travelling, but it -- I'm -- from my own point of view, I find myself slipping in efficiency. I'm very tired. I'm sorry about that. It's just the way it's happened. I am slipping a bit in efficiency and preparation. You've probably seen a bit of flapping at the bar table. It's in everyone's interest to finish today. I'd be prepared to go a little bit longer. I don't think I'll be very effective if I went too much longer, frankly, I'm -- I just find myself tired. I don't know whether the Court can accommodate that anyway, but I express a willingness to go some further distance if need be. I will try to finish by 1.30. But it's -- it's ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe I have to make any inquiry to see whether there even any other cases arranged for this courtroom this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes believe there isn't, but --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm checking now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. So could we have the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The courtroom is available, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Delalic. Okay. Now, the next passage I want to go -- I'm sorry. Before the break I was asking you questions about -- about page -- I'm not sure which page it was. But the section where this statement claims that an investigation should be conducted in connection with this incident. Could you now find out -- I say it's beginning: "That evening I went with Zuka to his apartment where we spent the night." Do you see that? It's at the same spot we were before but just after that. I'm sorry. Do you have -- can you see that, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I will -- we'll find it. It's the last part from this particular document that I want to go to. I'll just -- I'll hold it up. Can you see that green part there that I'm -- where the numbers 8, 8.30, that sort of number? There's a mark there, and there's 8 to 8.30 there.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which -- oh, all right. I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks. Okay. Now the passage I want to read out is the one that begins with the sentence: "That evening I went with Zuka to his apartment." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: "Where we spent the night. And in the morning" -- I just stop here. I'm butting my own words in here. It is apparent that this is after -- in your account after you have been to Grabovica and spoken to the soldiers and so on. And that evening you went with Zuka to his apartment "where we spent the night. And in the morning we got up sometime between 0800 and 0830 hours. And at around 0900 hours we were in his command in Donja Jablanica. In the command in Donja Jablanica I found Erdin Arnautovic, who was the logistics officers attached to my unit and who had just come from Grabovica to pick up the MTS for the unit. Dino said then that two children had been found between the houses in Grabovica. I returned to Grabovica with Dino in order to see the children." Now, Mr. Delalic, again, on this occasion you're saying -- on this occasion, I mean in this letter before Judge Hadzic you're saying that you went and spoke to the children on the morning of the 10th. Now that's different from your evidence in court here. Now, can I ask you: Why is that paragraph in your statement before Judge Hadzic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, most of the things that you've just stated are true. It's possible that as I was giving my statement, time was recorded inaccurately. But roughly speaking, all of this is true, what is reflected here, except I never gave the exact time. Well, maybe there was a bit of confusion. But when I found out that I was to testify before this Tribunal, I did prepare a little, needless to say. This after all, is an institution where you're in no position to lie and muck about. What I said before this Tribunal is true; that's all I can say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, could the witness please be shown D -- excuse me. It's Defence Exhibit D1560. This is uploaded and this is a document on the computer. It's Defence 65 ter number D1560 and it's a -- the ERN number is DD003254. It's a document that the -- we have a copy in Bosnian and in English for the Prosecutors because it's a bit of a lengthy document. And we have a copy also for Mr. Delalic to look at in hard copy because -- what I'm going to show now, Your Honours, is the judgement in a case against a man called Ismet Dahic in which this witness also figured as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Delalic, were you a witness in a prosecution of Ismet Dahic where he was accused of issuing you wrongfully with a passport when you weren't supposed to get one?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, sorry, could I just ask that this particular document be given an MFI number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be MFI 426.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, in this document could I just ask you to look at the section which is headed "statement of reasons."

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, on the -- on the e-court this is on page 3 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm not sure which page it is for you, but do you have "statement of reasons," that part?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. The second paragraph of that statement of reasons contains Dahic's defence. I'll just read it in and you read along with it. "The accused Ismet Dahic denied committing the crime and stated that he had not instructed either Sijad Sabitovic or anyone else to issue a passport to Ramiz Delalic. Since 1986 he had been following Ramiz Delalic and the crimes assigned to him -- ascribed to him," I'm sorry, "which was the year he directed and operation called T1, and he personally arrested him." And I'll point out that 1986 was probably a wrong date. "While Dahic was the person for the canton, Delalic had been detected as perpetrator of some five or six crimes which defies the logic. In the same year when he spearheaded a widespread campaign of combatting crime in the town, he as minister would order a passport to be issued to Ramiz Delalic. Therefore, he seized no grounds for Ramiz Delalic's charges against him." Now, have you read that passage?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, before I ask you anymore questions, the fact is that Dahic was an enemy of yours for many years. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Dahic was the person who besieged you and ultimately arrested you way on the on the 26th of October, 1993, during the Trebevic operation. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And isn't it also the case that Ismet Dahic was the person who you made the comment about breaking his legs with a baseball bat that I asked you about the other day. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, now to continue. If you could turn over the page now, it's about five or six paragraphs further. There's a sentence beginning with the name Zijad Sabitovic. Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'll go through it in just a minute, but I just wanted to ask you this: According to you Dahic did issue you a passport in his office in the way that he was charged. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you also made that claim in a newspaper article -- I'll show it to you if you need to, but you made that claim in a newspaper article, Oslobodjenje, which had the heading: "I am a man with glasses and a moustache but no beard." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Didn't you give an interview to Oslobodjenje at one stage where -- where you said that Dahic had indeed issued you with a passport and the photograph of you in that passport was a man with glasses and a moustache but no beard?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Ismet Dahic did issue me that passport in his office pursuant to an order from the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay, well that's fine, but -- now, let's go back to this paragraph here, this Zijad Sabitovic one. I'll read it with you. "Zijad Sabitovic indeed confirmed" -- I'll just pause here. And this -- I just have something for Your Honour's benefit and for the witness, too. You don't need to know the details of who Zijad Sabitovic were unless somebody else says that you do. It's really what comes afterwards that's important. "Zijad Sabitovic indeed confirmed that Sefer Sehodzic" -- sorry, "Sehovic," [phoen] I apologise for my mistakes, "had informed him that the boss," who is the accused, "requested a passport to be prepared for Ramiz Delalic. But this part of his statement was not corroborated, either by Sehovic's same time or by Ramiz Delalic's statement. The latter changed his statement given during the investigation by claiming that he had no recollection of receiving the passport from Dahic, as he had said earlier. He also could not remember if he had ever been in the office of the accused, Ismet Dahic, because he had persistently refused to see him." And the court goes on to say this: "This view of the accused's defence argument and the indisputable fact that the accused Dahic had been involved on several occasions on detecting the crimes committed by Ramiz Delalic, the court decided to place faith in the statement given by Delalic at the trial in which he said that he had never had any contact with the accused." Now, Mr. Delalic, you lied to that court, didn't you, when you said you couldn't remember getting the passport from Dahic. True or false?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first thing, I was serving a six-month sentence at the time and the accusation I made was not only in relation to Ismet Dahic, but also to Suljagic, I think that was his name. The warden of the prison in which I was serving my sentence was a relative of this Suljagic whom I had accused. During my stay in the prison I was not treated the same way as all the other prisoners. Those prisoners serving their sentences had larger rooms, they could socialise, they could play certain games like chess, dominoes. Meanwhile, I was in my own room in isolation facing a lot of grief from the warden. I was under so much pressure in fact that I was escorted all the way from prison to court. What I stated in court later was under duress and this is something that should be easy enough for you to check, that things happened the way I have just described, I mean the things that happened in prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document for tender.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, no, go ahead. That's all right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never for a moment did I deny that. I just said I didn't remember. It was proved, after all, that he had issued me the passport. Everyone knew who his chief was, the chief of the section that issued passports. It was proved that the passport was issued in the presence of Ismet Dahic and pursuant to a request that had been made by Ismet Dahic; however, what I said, I said facing an enormous amount of pressure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I offer that document for tender. Now, could I turn, please, to the D -- sorry, there's another document now that I wish to show. The one I'm going to show now is the indictment concerning -- that might as well be returned now, that document, and I'll show you the indictment now concerning you in Trebevic -- sorry, pardon me, the judgement concerning you in the Trebevic matter. This is D776 and its -- its ERN number is DD003094. Sorry, Your Honours, we're going to provide a hard copy of this to the Prosecutors, too, because it's a bit lengthy. I presume might have this one, but, anyway, we've got it in court today so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, here is a judgement, Mr. Delalic, in which you were sentenced to three years' imprisonment. And what occurred there was that you were sentenced for one charge but you were found not guilty on a number of others. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was convicted here for failure to execute the order of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Of Ismet Dahic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the indictment stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, I just want to take you to some parts of this. Just excuse me. This is on page 6 of the English version, and it -- on your version it will be a number of pages in. It's in the statement of reasons, and there's a paragraph that begins with: "In his statement, witness Ismet Dahic said on the 26th of October he directly took part in the implementation of the plan." Do you have that part?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, it's the fact, isn't it, that Dahic told the court that: "Commander Ramiz Delalic was called upon to surrender weapons and leave the facility with his group." Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true. Immediately, that morning, they killed several fighters from various snipers and wounded several others, and civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Is it your allegation that the -- that the forces involved in Trebevic -- in the Trebevic operation killed some civilians? Is that your claim?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, not civilians, fighters.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Excuse me, counsel. May it please Your Honour. I just had a quick look at this document which has been provided to us. I believe since the person here has been acquitted of all the other charges except insubordination and counsel here is asking about what a particular witness said, I think that if counsel would confine his arguments to the findings of the court as opposed to what one witness, because the court could have believed that witness or not, especially since there has been an acquittal. But to say that this witness said this, I don't think it's probative enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I believe this judgement and whatever's mentioned in it is just a clue to certain points, and the Prosecution makes that objection. But however, I believe Defence is entitled to ask those questions so long as those questions are relevant and has the probative value.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, could I -- yes, I will -- and I understand what my friend's saying. On pages 9 and 10, you can see the court's findings of fact so that what my friend says is right. I just say this for the transcript because I don't want to read the whole lot into the -- on pages 9 and 10 you can see the court's finding of fact. So what my friend says is right, some acquittals, one convictions, but the actual findings of fact and the analysis of the witnesses by the court cane be found, so I won't obviously go outside what the court -- what the court found.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Anyway, going back to what you recall about this and what Dahic said, is it the fact that Dahic makes accusation against you: "In the meantime Ramiz Delalic rounded up civilians from the neighbouring buildings and brought them to fire on premises" -- sorry. Pardon me. That was a ... "In the meantime Ramiz Delalic rounded up civilians from the surrounding villages and brought them to his base where they were used as hostages to prevent a firearms attack on his building." Now, that's an allegation that Dahic made at the time. Let me ask you this question: That's true, sit, you did bring those people as hostages?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said, during the attack against us there had been no warning. Right at the beginning, eight soldiers were wounded. Some gravely, some had minor wounds, some were critically wounded. A vast amount of various artillery rounds were fired on us with some kind of a gas. It was during that time that several people from nearby buildings looked for shelter in the barracks. There was none of what you are claiming, taking civilians and hostages or anything like that. No civilians were used for any of those purposes. It was that the civilians looked for shelter in the barracks because there was so much smoke. There were many children there. The soldiers who were in the barracks did not have enough protective masks to give to the children. Children started throwing up, women and so on. Everything was engulfed in the smoke. So these people took shelter in a room within the barracks, and then they remained within that room throughout the attack during which gas was used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, on page 9 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did the court find against you in the following terms --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is page 9, it's in the middle, it's after a huge clump of names included Haravak [phoen], Sabovic, Kajevic, Krluca [phoen], and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did the court say this: "The court completely accepted allegations presented by the defence, as these allegations were confirmed in the statements by witnesses Ismet Dahic." Sorry, I probably should have introduced what I was getting at there, so I apologise. Just disregard that. It's the fact, isn't it, that you, even as early as 9.00 in the morning, were in telephone contact with Ismet Dahic. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked to speak on the phone with Mr. Vahid Karavelic, however Ismet Dahic picked up the phone. I don't know whether you have the transcript of that conversation. On that occasion, I asked him to halt the attack. And the soldiers who were in the barracks, the civilians, the children, I asked for them to be moved out of the barracks. We didn't know what was going on. Nobody had informed us about any kind of attack or anything like that. Therefore, I asked Ismet Dahic to move out the civilians and the fighters, some of whom were gravely wounded. To that he replied he would set everything on fire and destroy everything. You probably have that conversation recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On the bottom of page 10 in the English version, Your Honour, about five lines from the bottom. Mr. Delalic, did the court make a finding in the following terms: "The court completely accepted statements by witnesses Ismet Dahic and Rusmir Mokavic [phoen], as both are convincing, logical, and circumstantial, and they give no rise to doubts." Is that a finding that the court made?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: During the -- the prosecutor played you a tape of the conversation that you had with Sefer Halilovic on the 26th of October. But I want to put to you that there was more than one such conversation, and in fact that you spoke to Sefer on three or more than three occasions on that day. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I spoke to him a couple of times. I don't know how many times we talked, but more than once.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in fairness to you, I think you indicated this earlier that Sefer Halilovic wasn't the only person you spoke to on the phone that day by any means. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I also spoke with the president, Mr. Alija Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you've indicated Dahic. Did you also speak to Ejub Ganic at any time?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As this fact was established, namely that many of the civilians who were there were poisoned by the gas used against us and the civilians, they sent in a delegation to the barracks. The then-prime minister, Hari Suljagic was a member of that delegation, as was the army commander - at the time that was Rasim Delic - the then-MUP minister, Alispahic, Ismet Dahic, and some other people were in that delegation but I can't recall that now. On that occasion, the civilians who were in the office close to mine spat at the delegation, precisely because of the way in which they reacted and because of the type of attack that was used against the civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did -- at about 2.00 in the afternoon, 1400 hours, did you have a conversation with Sefer Halilovic in the following terms, and I'll put it to you. You said: "Boss, they've issued an ultimatum saying they would attack in five minutes." Sefer said: "Who?" And you said: "You know, fuck it." And Sefer said: "Who issued the ultimatum?" And you said: "I don't know, I'm calling Alija because I said to stop shooting and he said he would call them and tell them. And now it seems he went to the corps." And Sefer said: "Who?" You said: "Alija." He said: "The president?" And you said: "Yeah." Sefer said: "Ganic just called and said to tell him to surrender and later we would see what to do. I said I would pass it on so there were no problems. That was just now. I finished talking to him three minutes ago. Here is Ganic's phone number, 472-618. And you said: "Okay, boss." And Sefer said: "Okay." Now, did you have that conversation with Sefer Halilovic at about 2.00 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible. I had several conversations with him. I really can't remember this specific one. I was beside myself with everything that was going on. It's possible that we had this conversation, but I really can't say for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, I've got some other questions --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, could that Trebevic judgement please be given a number as well? I offer it -- that for tender.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document is marked 4 -- MFI 427.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm very grateful for that. Very well. Thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, finally I have some questions for you concerning what you -- some of the matters you raised when you first gave evidence here. You said in evidence here that you got special financial support from Sefer Halilovic at the time when he was the commander of the army, and you mentioned a person named Dika, his chef de cabinet. Now, I put to you that Dika stopped working for him in February of 1993. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: February 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the documents indicate, but whenever I came to see Sefer Halilovic I found her either in the office, where she usually was, or in his bed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, all right. Isn't it the fact that there was a person there named Safet Baltic who had the duty of issuing money from the safe and keeping records of such monies?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never received money from this person called Safet Baltic. I don't know who that person is. I'm sure I never met this person. All the money I ever got was from Sefer or from Dika. In most cases it was Dika who would issue me money because she had been ordered to do so by Sefer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But it's the fact, isn't it, that any monies you were issued to from Sefer's office were properly documented and were given to you for the purposes of arms purchases, and in fact you used them for such purposes. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, it wasn't just my brigade that was receiving money; there were other brigades, too. The 1st Mountain Brigade, for example; there was the 10th Mountain Unit; the Delta Unit; and my brigade. I'm sure there must be certificates and receipts to that effect, but sometimes there was no receipt issued. It all depended on how urgently the money was needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no. Now, just on that topic of no receipts being issued, there was nothing sinister or sneaky about that, was there? You've indicated that that was just when it was an urgent matter. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. So when you make a claim that -- that your brigade was treated with preference by Sefer Halilovic, that would be reflected or not reflected, depending on the truth of your claim, in those records. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: So that if Mr. Safet Baltic were to say that the 9th Mountain Brigade was not in any kind of privileged position in relation to the acquirement of financial means, you couldn't dispute that, could you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, maybe not the 9th Mountain Brigade, I'm not sure which brigade we're talking about. But the 9th Motorised Brigade did have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, yes, you're right to correct me there, I suppose. You got me. Your -- the brigade of which you were the deputy commander, I put to you, did not have any preferential treatment and you've disagreed with me on that. I'll move on. Next of all, you would agree, Mr. Delalic, that you were not in the line of the rick [phoen], in the line of command and control of the army? You didn't regard yourself as bound by that. Would you agree with me about that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I, or my unit, rather the 9th Motorised Brigade, the unit that I was a member of, was within the command system. There is no order indicated that this unit was anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you know any armies in the world or any military rules in the world that provide for a soldier being in the system of command and control when they're conspiring to murder the commander-in-chief?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You must know that none of the armies in the world that you referred to is like the army that there was in Bosnia and Herzegovina, besieged on all sides, entirely surrounded. And there was anarchy among its ranks. It wasn't possible to establish an army to resemble the armies that you're talking about, to even bear a distant resemblance to any of those armies. I'm not sure this is what I should tell you. This is the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, maybe you can tell me this. Why was it that you waited until you came to The Hague to make this claim that Sefer was in a conspiracy with you and the Deltas to murder Rasim Delic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, in a way it is my opinion that there was never a direct order to kill those civilians. I'm positive about that. If you ask me, the soldiers who did that should have been sentenced, although to some extent I consider Sefer Halilovic responsible because he failed to take certain steps and all that. What I mean to say is: This institution, this Tribunal, that at least is my opinion, is a Tribunal where one should under no circumstances lie. I am convinced that the investigators of this Tribunal are privy to every little detail and everything else that occurred in Grabovica. I have no need to lie or to muck about. I am certain that the only thing one is supposed to do is tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. You, just excuse me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would Your Honours just give me one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I just want to approach the accused briefly, if I might.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I've got a question about communications now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You've indicated you don't think you had Motorolas with you in -- in Konjic. How did you communicate with Grabovica at the time when, according to your story, you got down to -- down to Jablanica and heard this news and then you came back and saw Sefer Halilovic and then you heard news about the boys being found. Now, I want to ask you: What's the form of communications that was used to give you that piece of information?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I could not remember whether we got Motorolas later on or not. But from the time I arrived, from Konjic to Jablanica, when I arrived in Zuka's base, it was then that I learned about the crime that had happened. I did not learn about the crime while I was in Konjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. I just want to put --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I referred to a Safet Baltic document before, and I just want to have that distributed now. It's a bit lengthy to read into the transcript in the time that we've got, but I can put the main parts of it to the witness. Okay. I'll start reading it now while it's circulating, if that's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: You're -- this is what the letter says: "I, Safet Baltic," and it gives some details. He says: "I was appointed as a member of staff in July 1992 for the collection of the means for the defensive needs of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and in accordance with the order of the Chief of Staff of the armed forces. I was appointed as leader and as the one responsible for the treasury of the foreigner currency means and the treasury for special purposes of the staff of the supreme command of the OS BiH. As a person who had the exclusive right to guard and to issue the foreign currency means upon an order of the chief of the SVK of the OS BiH, I guarded those capably and very responsibly and would issue the same upon mentioned oral or written orders. I state responsibly that at the time there was no possibility" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I will slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: "I state responsibly at the time there was no possibility of such abuse of the financial resources from the treasury of the SVK OS BiH nor was there the theoretical possibility for such abuse. All the means are orderly documented and justified in accordance with the possibilities that were available in the time of war. It is familiar to me that the mean -- that means were given to units and commands of the ABiH in accordance with the possibilities where they were the most needed, according to the estimates. I remember that in the period the 9th Brigade was given 60.000 Deutschmarks and that these means were exclusively used for the purchase and transporting of the MTS in the besieged Sarajevo. The 9th Mountain Brigade of the ABiH was not in any kind of privileged position in relation to the acquirement of financial means." And the witness then -- sorry, well, Mr. Baltic then goes on to give details of other units which are included there. Now, the fact is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I offer for that document for tender, first of all. It falls into the same category as the other ones -- other letters that we've put to you in the last week in response to what's been said in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Chana.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm a bit confused as to this way of doing things. Your Honour, these are people obviously who have communicated to the Defence. While Defence is entitled to put to this witness some of the things that have been said to get his answer because he is in court today, I don't think that these can be introduced into evidence. The Defence, during their Defence case, of course, may bring forward these witnesses, we can cross-examine them, and Your Honours will have the benefit of the full testimony of these witnesses. But to tender these into -- as exhibits, Your Honour, the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll deal with the document issues at a later stage, maybe by the paper communications.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But anyway, I believe that the Defence counsel is entitled to ask this witness whether the 9th Mountain Brigade was in a more favourable position in terms of receiving money compared with other units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, Mr. Delalic, what I put to you is this: To the extent that the 9th Brigade had an advantage over other brigades, it's because you were able to get voluntary donations from the cafe owners and other business people in the old town where you were based. That's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Firstly, I would like to know something. This document does not say that the units of which I was a member ever received any money at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, it does. You must have missed it, but you received 60.000 Deutschmarks.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't see it anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, we'll have to check. That could be a -- be the -- an interpretation problem, but --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is nothing on the face of this document to indicate that my unit ever received any money at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, do you see a sentence there saying: "I remember that in that period the 9th Brigade was given 60.000 Deutschmarks"?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's talk here of the 9th Mountain Brigade -- no, there is an enormous difference, the difference between the 9th Mountain Brigade on the one hand and the 109th Motorised Brigade on the other. What this shows is that this person was not privy to these details at all. Perhaps he didn't even know who he gave the money to, if indeed he had given any money at all. And believe me, he wasn't there when the money was handed over, whenever money was received, it was either from Dika or from Sefer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, now the question is this: Did you know that at the start of June of 1993, Mustafa Hajrulahovic, Talijan, and Sefer Halilovic approached the Presidency and asked for you to be replaced, you and Caco to be replaced. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, just to conclude this cross-examination now, I want to put something to you. You weren't really in a particularly close relationship with Sefer Halilovic at all, but rather he was just a superior officer that you liked and admired in the fight that you were both fighting against the aggressor. Isn't that the fact?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Sefer Halilovic and I were on exceptionally friendly terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: He was just your superior officer and he was friendly to you just like he was friendly to other officers who were fighting bravely in the army. Isn't that the real truth, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Those are the questions. Thank you for your attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Any re-examination, Ms. Chana?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. I'll deal with this last document first. Your Honour ...

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Mr. Delalic, you have the Bosnian document there and I have the English translation. Could you read from the sentence: "I remember that in that period," and then if you read that, please. What exactly does it say? Can you find it? It's like towards the end -- just before all that money stuff starts coming up.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I remember that in that period, the 9th Mountain Brigade of the BH army was given about 60.000 German marks. This money was used in order to bring into the besieged Sarajevo materiel and technical equipment. The 9th Mountain Brigade was in no" --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: That's fine for my purposes --

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Because, Your Honour, I notice this the English translation it says -- the word "Motorised Brigade" has been left out -- sorry. The word 9th -- "mountain" is not in the English translation. The English translation Your Honour, it says "9th Brigade."

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: You wouldn't know that because you don't read English, but in your -- the question to you, Mr. Delalic, would be that "Mountain" is a word reflected in the Bosnian version. Is that correct? If you could confirm that for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. 9th Mountain Brigade of the BH army. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And that would be a different brigade than the 9th Motorised Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a huge difference, both in terms of their respective strength and in terms of weapons they had, the number of battalions, everything else. It's worlds apart. The mountain brigade on the one hand and the motorised brigade on the other.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And just to confirm again, Mr. Delalic, you are the deputy commander of the 9th Motorised Brigade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Now, the last set of questions counsel for the Defence asked you is -- and that document was shown to you to say that money was given equally to each brigade. Now, my question to you, Mr. Delalic, is: Why did Sefer Halilovic treat -- did -- sorry. Did Sefer Halilovic treat you the same way as other brigades, as other brigade commanders?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, the chef de cabinet of the chief of the Main Staff should at least have the rank of colonel or general. They should be familiar with the fundamental differences between the mountain brigade, the mechanised brigade, and the motorised brigade. He wasn't familiar with these concepts. He probably wasn't around, and that's why he doesn't know when the money was distributed. As I said, the units of the 9th Motorised Brigade enjoyed a position that was much more privileged than the other units, the units of the 9th Motorised Brigade, alongside with the Delta Unit, was foremost among the units. In Sarajevo, there were many ways for units to obtain weapons. Weapons were, for the most part, distributed to these units. So there again, these units were privileged because they were receiving most of the weapons, the 9th Motorised Brigade and the Delta Unit. There were a great many ways to deliver weapons to Sarajevo. I don't wish to go into that subject now, but there you have it. The gist of the whole matter is that most of the weapons ended up in these two units.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: And why was that, Mr. Delalic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, there was a lot of discord and a number of changes - I'm talking about late 1992 and 1993 - in the various corps and in the Main Staff itself. There were a number of officers who wanted to keep strong units until the moment of decision came.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, Mr. -- Learned counsel for the Defence showed you a letter written by Sadika Omerbegovic. Now, can you tell me, was she always present when this money was handed out to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, there was a joke going around at Dika's expense in the army. It was always being said that Dika was the true commander and Mr. Halilovic her deputy. Every time money was distributed, every time money was earmarked by the command, for whatever purpose, Dika was always there and so was Mr. Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Now, when you were given this money, these various amounts that you testified to earlier when I was examining you before learned Defence counsel, did you ever sign any receipt yourself acknowledging receipt of these monies?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am positive that I did not obtain any receipt ever from this man, Safet Baltic, but I'm equally certain that the investigators must be in possession of some receipts issued by Dika, something signed by her or by Sefer Halilovic. I do believe that I myself signed one or two of those.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: So there would be occasion then, Mr. Delalic, that you would sign for this money which you got?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Would there also be occasions when you didn't sign for the money that you got?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Just to be quite clear about it, what would be the procedures generally when any commander received money from the supreme staff?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, normally a receipt would indicate the amount of money issued, and normally that would be done by the assistant commander for finance. However, in these instances I personally went to take the money.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Were you -- on those occasions -- I'm not talking about the occasions when you signed a receipt or on the occasions when you did not sign a receipt, were you -- did you ever -- did you ever ask to sign one? How would you take the money?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've already said, I would normally go to Sefer, ask him for a certain amount of money. He would tell Dika to give me the money and I would receive the money. The adjacent office to his belonged to Dika, the safe was there. She was the one who worked with the safe, and she would give me whatever I requested in order to buy weapons. So sometimes a receipt was issued and signed by me, but sometimes it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Now, I'd like to take you to a document which was shown to you by -- by learned counsel for the Defence, which is P215, and this is a report to Jasarevic from Zankovic. Do you remember that or do need to see it again? Because -- I mean, just not to waste time, Your Honour, because in that report it was stated that Ramiz Delalic executed one of his soldiers. Do you remember that report? You can be shown it again, Mr. Delalic, if you are not quite clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, if it assists, I don't mind my learned friend reading the passage to the witness so that -- to remind him of what's being said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have seen this report already.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And we are familiar with those allegations. Here we just put a simple question to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Do you remember that, Mr. Delalic, when this particular report stated, this is Zankovic's report to Jasarevic saying that you executed a soldier, and this is obviously in connection with when you saw the Zadro brothers.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm not mistaken, that document contains two different allegations. One is that I shot one of my own soldiers, and the other is about the alleged murder of Ivica, a Croat, who was with Zulfikar. I'm not sure which one you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: I'm talking about you executing a soldier, and perhaps I should put entire question to you so as to be quite clear what direction I'm taking. Did you in fact execute a soldier; that's the question?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: So to that extent, the report would not be accurate. Is that -- would that be --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ DELALIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.
